narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed and, unfortunately, the assessment concluded that you present a higher-than-average risk of credit difficulties, with the model estimating a roughly 51% probability that you would struggle to repay the loan — just enough to tip the decision toward denial. While this is a borderline result, the system flagged several specific aspects of your financial profile that, taken together, raised enough concern to decline the application.

The single most influential factor working against you was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about one in five had a negative checking account balance, while the majority either had no account or maintained a positive balance. A negative checking account balance signals to the model that you may already be under financial strain, making it harder to take on additional debt responsibly.

Closely behind this, your credit history also raised a red flag. You were recorded as having no prior credits or having paid all credits elsewhere — a category that sounds positive on the surface, but is actually quite rare among approved applicants, representing only about 2% of those who were granted loans. The vast majority of approved applicants had a history of existing credits that were paid on time, or even some past credit difficulties that were resolved. Paradoxically, having no credit footprint at this bank makes it harder to assess your reliability as a borrower, and the model interpreted this as a risk factor.

On a more positive note, your property ownership — specifically your real estate — worked in your favor, partially offsetting the concerns above. Owning real estate is a meaningful sign of financial stability, and this factor pushed the model's assessment in a more favorable direction, though not enough to overcome the other concerns.

It is also worth noting that your installment rate of 4% of disposable income is higher than the average of about 2.94% among approved applicants, and you already have two existing credits at this bank compared to an average of about 1.4 among approved applicants — both of which suggest your financial obligations are already relatively stretched.

As a next step, you are encouraged to work on building a clearer and more established credit history, ideally by taking on smaller, manageable credit products and repaying them consistently. Bringing your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying would also significantly strengthen your profile. Speaking directly with a bank advisor could help you understand what specific improvements would make the most difference, and given how close this decision was, even modest changes to your financial situation could lead to a different outcome in the future.
